title: MakeMyTrip Files Confidentially for India IPO, Could Raise Over $1 Billion
excerpt: MakeMyTrip files for a confidential IPO in India, aiming to raise over $1 billion.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • MakeMyTrip files for a confidential IPO in India, aiming to raise over $1 billion.
  • The IPO will consist entirely of an offer for sale of equity shares.
  • MakeMyTrip's FY26 profit fell 45.8% to $51.7 million, despite revenue growth.
  • NRI investors may benefit from dual listing and cross-market trading opportunities.
  • MakeMyTrip follows Yatra as the second Indian travel tech company to list in both markets.
IPO Details and Implications
›Confidential filing with SEBI for India IPO.
›IPO could raise over $1 billion.
›Entirely an offer for sale of equity shares.
›Enhances brand visibility for MakeMyTrip.

NASDAQ-Listed Travel Giant Eyes India Listing

MakeMyTrip, India's largest online travel company, has confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for the India IPO of its subsidiary, MakeMyTrip (India) Limited.

The company, already listed on NASDAQ since 2010, revealed the filing in a regulatory submission to the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Reports suggest the IPO could raise over $1 billion through an offer for sale (OFS), making it one of the most anticipated India listings of the year.

How the IPO Will Work

The IPO will consist entirely of an OFS of equity shares by MakeMyTrip Ltd and its Singapore-based subsidiary ibibo Group Holdings (GoIbibo), which MakeMyTrip acquired in October 2016 in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $720 million.

The India-listed entity will continue as a subsidiary of NASDAQ-listed MakeMyTrip. Following the IPO, MakeMyTrip may explore alternatives allowing shareholders to trade securities that are "fungible and listed across India and US capital markets."

"MakeMyTrip expects the proposed IPO and listing to enhance its brand visibility and support MMT India's ability to incentivise and promote talent in a competitive technology recruitment landscape," the company said.

Financial Picture and Strategic Moves

Ahead of the filing, MakeMyTrip restructured its brands, merging subsidiary RedBus with its Indian entity. It has also acquired minority stakes in visa processing platform Atlys and holiday packages company Flamingo Transworld.

MakeMyTrip's FY26 profit declined 45.8 percent year-over-year to $51.7 million, while revenue grew 6.7 percent to $1.04 billion. For Q4 FY26, profit fell 16.8 percent to $24.3 million on revenue of $250.1 million. Investment banks including Axis Capital, Morgan Stanley, and JP Morgan are among the company's advisers.

What It Means for NRI Investors

For the Indian diaspora, MakeMyTrip's dual listing creates a unique opportunity. NRI investors who rely on the NASDAQ listing could soon hold shares through Indian exchanges, potentially with fungible cross-market trading. The company's brand recognition among overseas Indians — who use MakeMyTrip extensively for booking flights, hotels, and rail tickets — makes it one of the most personally relevant IPOs for the diaspora.

MakeMyTrip would become the second Indian travel tech company to list in both the US and India, following Yatra.

Sources: Inc42, SEC filings
